description: Bio (personal intro) and role (job description) scripts for each Operational Specialist. Each script is ~50-150 words to keep ElevenLabs cost and playback length manageable. Read by netlify/functions/tg-voice.js, which pairs the script with the voice_id from helpers_master.json. An office with a role but no bio simply has no bio audio.

ms_ivy.bio: I'm Ms. Ivy. I came to libraries the hard way. When I was a kid my mom got sick, and the wall of medical papers between me and understanding her illness felt impossible at first. So I taught myself to work through them. By my twenties I was teaching others to do the same. Then I went to school for library and information sciences and specialized in health. The skillset travels. The questions change, the method doesn't.
ms_ivy.role: I'm The Librarian. I work two paths. If you don't have an idea yet, tell me your world, what frustrates you, and what you'd bring to the table. I run my method, map the space around your topic, find the real gaps, and hand you back three idea candidates. If you already have an idea, I run a different search - I find the academic frameworks behind it, the adjacent thinkers worth reading, the prior literature, and the actual research gap your idea sits in. Both paths end the same way. You leave with something specific you can walk into the Chamber with.
ms_ivy.intro: Welcome. I'm Ms. Ivy, the librarian. You're here because you don't have an idea yet, and that's exactly what I'm for. Tell me three things. Your world. What frustrates you in it. What you'd bring to the table. I run the search. I hand you back three candidates. You pick the one that feels right. Then it walks through The Gauntlet.

dr_rao_opsec.bio: I spent eight years in systems analysis before I understood that the most dangerous version of any technology is never the intended one. It's the adjacent one. The one nobody designed for but someone will find. I mapped my first dual use risk matrix for a public health surveillance platform that was, under the right conditions, a targeting system. That's when I stopped thinking about intended use and started thinking about all the others.
dr_rao_opsec.role: I run the dual use risk analysis between Ms. Ivy and the Specialist offices. Eight passes. Repurposing vectors, misuse pathways, adversarial reinterpretation, environmental triggers, and four more. At the end I issue a determination. GO or NO-GO. No middle position. If the dual use risk is structurally embedded, the concept goes back to Ms. Ivy for restructuring. If it can be managed, it moves forward. The risk map I produce travels with your concept into every Specialist office.

iris_king_opsec.role: I run the Office of Frontline Communications. I evaluate how your concept speaks to the public, to customers, and to anyone who makes first contact with it. We examine every surface where a stranger interacts with what you have built, and I identify where your language reveals more than it should and where it invites the wrong questions. You leave with a controlled communication surface, language guidance for each first-contact point, and the specific openings closed. Adversaries start with questions. My job is to stop you handing them the questions.

alicia_james_opsec.role: I run the Office of Structure and Compliance. I evaluate whether your concept is structurally aligned with how it actually operates - entity type, ownership, the documentation that governs it, and the registrations and licenses it requires versus the ones it has. That gap is your exposure. This is not legal advice; it is structural analysis. You leave with an alignment assessment, a clarified compliance posture, and an inventory of the points where your structure can be challenged or pierced, ranked by severity. The sector chiefs will find those gaps. I find them first.

kimberly_pass_opsec.role: I run the Office of Legal Surface Review. I read legal surfaces - not as your attorney, as your researcher. Most operational failures begin with a document someone did not read, a term someone assumed applied, or a regulatory requirement someone did not know existed. I read those documents, find those terms, and surface those requirements. You leave with a legal question map organised by domain, the specific areas that need licensed review, and the document gaps closed before the sector chiefs get to them. I do not give you answers. I give you the right questions to bring to counsel.

sasha_moreno_opsec.role: I run the Office of Human Factors and Insider Risk. I map who has access to what, at what level, and under what conditions - built for the concept as it actually operates, not as it was ideally imagined. You leave with a secure human architecture, explicit access levels for each role, and an inventory of the insider threat vectors in your current structure, ranked by severity. I will name the uncomfortable one. In most early-stage concepts the largest insider risk is the founder, and it is better to hear that from me than from a sector chief trained in human factors.

leo_vance_opsec.role: I run the Office of Financial Exposure. I put the financial structure of your concept under realistic pressure and find where it holds and where it breaks - named specifically, not hypothetically. You leave with a stress-tested model, an inventory of concentration risks, vendor dependencies and cash flow vulnerabilities ranked by the damage each would cause, and a plain-language picture of what this concept can absorb and what it cannot. I am not here to admire your projections. I am here to find the seam before the chiefs do.

rowan_tate_opsec.role: I run the Office of Risk Discipline and Guardrails. I map risk structurally rather than as a list of worst cases - a ranked inventory of vulnerabilities with the evidence behind each one. You leave with a risk architecture assessment, a guardrail gap report naming every place you are operating without a safety floor and the minimum control that would close it, and a confidence reality check. That last one is the useful part: a plain statement of where your confidence is supported by evidence and where it has outrun it. The sector chiefs will probe exactly those gaps.

jax_rivera_opsec.role: I run the Office of Information Exposure and Discoverability. Your digital footprint is already out there. I map every public-facing element of your concept - what is indexed, what is discoverable, and what a motivated competitor or adversary would find in a thirty-minute open-source search. You leave with an exposure surface inventory, a strategic disclosure timeline covering what should be public now, what waits for a trigger event and what should never be published, and an assessment of your domain and brand surface. I run the search before they do.

yuki_mendel_opsec.role: I run the Office of Visual Surface and Brand Security. I assess what your visual identity communicates before anyone speaks - typography, colour, mark, and system coherence, category by category. You leave with a visual signal audit showing where the signals are accurate and where they introduce doubt, a credibility gap report ranking the places implementation falls below the register you are claiming, and a briefing on the visual surface as the sector chiefs will read it. The room draws a conclusion about your concept from its visual identity before you open your mouth.

ali_malik_opsec.role: I run the Office of Threat Attribution and Subject Analysis, the last desk before findings are consolidated. I assemble the public picture of the presenter the way a motivated sector chief or competitive analyst would assemble it. You leave with a subject intelligence report, a contradiction map naming every place the public record conflicts with your pitch narrative, and a pre-Chamber exposure briefing covering what to address proactively, what to leave alone, and what to have an answer ready for. I show you the picture. What you do with it is yours.
